decisions.what: Hexagon rings are written clockwise (30, 330, 270, 210, 150, 90, 30 degrees) and vertices clamped to lon +-180 and lat +-90
decisions.why: Plotly geo (d3-geo) treats counter-clockwise rings, and cells crossing the antimeridian or a pole, as the whole globe minus the cell; the first screenshot filled the whole map

decisions.what: globalRules only sets HOVER[tr.type] when the trace has no hovertemplate
decisions.why: The generic choropleth template would overwrite the hex hover '%{z:,} points'

decisions.what: main.py dashboard passes geo = _appview(d, f, 'map') when the Map app is shown
decisions.why: The template needs chart-1 (shown, total, rule) to render the figure macro; the lru_cache makes the later /app call reuse it

decisions.what: scrollZoom false for map2d via a per-chart copy of CONFIG
decisions.why: DESIGN.md: wheel zoom stays off on the map; other figures (3D) keep Plotly defaults

decisions.what: tableOf handles scattergeo (lon, lat, z_label) and the hex choropleth (centre lon, lat, Points per cell)
decisions.why: The table toggle runs on every figure and would throw on these trace types

tried_and_failed.what: Hex ring in the order 30, 90, ..., 330 degrees
tried_and_failed.why_it_failed: Counter-clockwise winding makes Plotly fill the whole globe for every cell

tried_and_failed.why_it_failed: It was off-screen or an edge cell; the test now hovers the middle cell after scrolling into view
